evidence: src/domain/task-status.ts defines TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus. This is the only definition of the status vocabulary in the module.
src/domain/task.ts imports TaskStatus from ./task-status and enforces the done-once rule only in Task.markDone(), which throws TaskAlreadyDoneError.
src/domain/errors.ts declares TaskAlreadyDoneError extends DomainError. This is one place for the error message of the done-once rule.
src/domain/task-repository.ts reuses TaskStatus for TaskFilter.status instead of redefining status literals.
src/domain/project-repository.ts, src/domain/user-repository.ts and src/domain/task-repository.ts follow the same save/findById port shape for the entities in project.ts, user.ts and task.ts.
src/domain/id-generator.ts declares an IdGenerator port with next(): string. Identity generation is abstracted, and no entity generates its own IDs.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module holds a single concern: the task-management domain model. It has three entities (Project, User, Task), a repository port for each (ProjectRepository, UserRepository, TaskRepository), an IdGenerator port, the task-status value set, and a domain error hierarchy. The abstractions are used consistently. Each repository interface follows the same save/findById shape, and TaskRepository adds a task-specific query (findByProjectId with TaskFilter). The status vocabulary is defined once in task-status.ts (TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus, isTaskStatus). Task.ts and task-repository.ts both import that type instead of redefining status literals. The rule that a completed task cannot be completed again lives only in Task.markDone, and its error lives only in errors.ts (TaskAlreadyDoneError extends DomainError). No file duplicates an invariant, works around the module's own types, or brings in an unrelated concern.
